findings.title: The lease declares business use, the insurance is rated personal
findings.detail: Page 7 of the lease carries a signed corporate declaration: the vehicle will be used primarily for business or commercial purposes. The preauthorized payment authorisation on the same page is ticked business purposes. Both insurance certificates rate the car as personal use, with the business kilometre field blank and the payment schedule marked Personal.
findings.why: An insurer that finds the declared use wrong can deny a claim on the whole policy, not just adjust the premium. This is the largest uninsured exposure on the file and it costs nothing to fix.
findings.action: Settle the real business use percentage, then correct the rating with Desjardins or disclose it to the brokers before anyone binds.

findings.title: Platinum Security may already be void for the same reason
findings.detail: Section 3.4 of the Platinum AutoPlus agreement makes a vehicle used for commercial or business purposes an Ineligible Vehicle, with no entitlement to any service. The lease declares exactly that use.
findings.why: $349 was paid for theft compensation worth up to $7,000 that may not be payable. The 30 day cancellation window closed on 30 October 2025, so the only move left is to establish in writing whether the agreement stands.
findings.action: Put the question to First Canadian Protection Products at 1-800-381-2580 in writing, quoting agreement AP-12876238.

findings.title: A minor conviction appeared between the two certificates
findings.detail: The 2025-26 certificate shows no convictions in the past three years. The 2026-27 renewal shows one minor. Nothing else in the rating changed: same territory 717, same rate groups, same driving record 6, same 3% winter tyre discount.
findings.why: The opening emails to all four brokers said no claims or convictions, ever. An undisclosed conviction discovered at bind is a misrepresentation.
findings.action: Pull the abstract from ServiceOntario for $12, then correct the disclosure in writing with all four brokers.

findings.title: The deductible ceiling is about $5,223, not $2,500
findings.detail: The lease requires a maximum deductible of $2,500 or 5% of the price of the vehicle, whichever is greater. Five percent of the $104,459.95 leased vehicle amount is $5,223. The separate Agreement to Furnish Insurance drops the tie breaker and reads as though $2,500 were the cap.
findings.why: Collision and comprehensive sit at $1,000 each, costing $3,401 combined on the renewal. There is contractual room to take a much higher deductible if a quote prices it well.
findings.action: Ask each broker to price collision and comprehensive at $2,500 alongside the $1,000 they will quote by default.

findings.title: The lease already carries gap protection
findings.detail: Section 13 of the lease provides gap protection as standard. On a total loss the insurance proceeds clear the lease balance and the only amounts still owed are the deductible, arrears, breach amounts and prorated excess kilometre charges. MBFS must be consulted before any actual cash value settlement is agreed, or the protection is forfeited.
findings.why: It changes what the $794 5 Year New Vehicle Protection is actually buying. It is not gap cover. It buys a new current year replacement car instead of a cash settlement, which is a different and more valuable thing, and it is the reason a cheaper quote carrying plain OPCF 43R is a downgrade.
findings.action: Do not let any broker sell separate gap or loan protection coverage. Ask instead whether their carrier offers true new vehicle replacement.

findings.title: Front tyres are 0.8 mm above the lease return threshold
findings.detail: The 12 August 2026 inspection read 4 mm at both front wheels and 5 mm at the rear. The lease counts tyres with less than 3.2 mm tread remaining as excess wear and tear. Tyres are also excluded from the prepaid maintenance plan.
findings.why: Replacement is at the lessee's expense either way, and summer performance tyres on 21 inch AMG wheels are not cheap. Worth planning rather than discovering at return.
findings.action: Recheck the tread at the next service and budget for front tyres before lease maturity on 30 September 2028.

findings.title: The payment method really did change, and the certificates disagree about when
findings.detail: The 2025-26 certificate as issued says method of payment Invoice, payable in full on receipt, $8,410 due 1 November 2025. The renewal's billing table shows that same term running at $700.84 monthly. So it converted to preauthorized debit partway through the term rather than at renewal.
findings.why: Only that the year over year comparison should describe two different billing arrangements, not one amount changing.
findings.action: None. Recorded so the 2025-26 figures are not read as monthly from the start.

findings.title: Two documents disagree on the warranty expiry
findings.detail: The lease pricing worksheet states MB 4 years or 80,000 km, which puts expiry at 29 September 2029. The dealer invoice prints a warranty expiry of 29 September 2028.
findings.why: The steering clock spring noise is unrepaired and being monitored. Which date governs decides how long that stays free to fix.
findings.action: Ask Mercedes-Benz Mississauga to confirm the governing warranty end date and get it in writing.

findings.title: No certificate names MBFS as loss payee, which the lease requires
findings.detail: Section 12 of the lease requires MBFS listed as Additional Named Insured and Loss Payee for comprehensive, fire, theft and collision, and as Additional Named Insured for liability. On both certificates the Lienholders box, headed to whom loss may be jointly payable, is blank. MBFS appears in the Lessor field and in the named insured block of the liability slips. OPCF 5 is on the policy, which extends coverage to the specified lessee.
findings.why: Whether the Lessor field plus OPCF 5 satisfies a loss payee requirement is an insurer practice question, not something the certificate settles. If it does not, a physical damage cheque could be issued without MBFS on it, and section 12 makes a failure to maintain the required insurance an immediate default under the lease.
findings.action: Ask Desjardins to confirm in writing that MBFS is recorded as loss payee for the physical damage coverages, and have it added if it is not. Put the same requirement to every broker as a condition of any replacement quote.

marketAssessment.verdict: Sound lease structure, thin discount on the car.
marketAssessment.summary: The residual protects you and the rate is market consistent for an AMG. What was left on the table was left at the negotiating table: a 1.89% discount, $5,107 of soft products and dealer fees, and a kilometre tier above what the car is driven.

comparables.description: GLC43 AMG Coupe, three years old

marketAssessment.comparablesNote: Dealer asking prices from AutoTrader.ca on 20 August 2026, not transaction prices. Real values sit below these.

strengths.point: The 58% residual is generous, and the market now says so
strengths.detail: Three year old GLC 43s ask $54,495 to $59,995 today. The guaranteed buyout is $58,580, at the top of that range. Mercedes-Benz Financial carries that depreciation risk, not the lessee.

strengths.point: 4.49% is consistent for an AMG variant
strengths.detail: A base 2026 GLC leases in Canada at 3.99% as of August 2026, and AMG models carry a premium with less subvention. No published Canadian residual and rate sheet for the AMG GLC 43 as of September 2025 could be found, so this is reasonable rather than verified.

strengths.point: Gap protection came free inside the lease
strengths.detail: Section 13 provides it as standard. Many buyers pay a dealer separately for the same thing.

weaknesses.detail: $2,076 off a $109,929.95 list. This is the weakest number in the file.

weaknesses.point: $5,107 of soft products and dealer fees
weaknesses.detail: A $695 administration fee, a $499 window tint, $170 wheel locks, and a prepaid maintenance plan at $1,779 which is exactly $480 plus $801 plus $498, the sum of its three retail services. No discount at all. It bought a fixed price, not a saving.

weaknesses.point: A kilometre tier above the car's actual use
weaknesses.detail: 18,000 a year bought against 15,871 driven. About 6,473 kilometres will go unused, and unused kilometres are never credited back.

maturity.recommendation: Walk away. Do not exercise the buyout.
maturity.why: The guaranteed price sits at the top of what three year old examples ask retail and roughly $8,500 above likely wholesale. A generous residual is worth having as protection, not as a purchase.

earlyExit.why: Section 16 charges the residual plus the balance of remaining payments on a constant yield discount, plus one further monthly payment, with any shortfall bearing 20% interest. Eleven months into a loaded German performance SUV the gap to trade value is at its widest.

nextTime: Negotiate the discount before anything else. It is the only number here worth thousands.
Decline the finance and insurance table, or price each product against buying it later.
Ask what the rate would be on the outgoing model year, which carries more subvention.
limits: Used listings are dealer asking prices, not transaction prices.
Today's three year old cars are a proxy for where a 2026 lands in 2028.
No published Canadian residual or subvented rate sheet for the AMG GLC 43 in September 2025 was found.
